question: Can whole forked rollouts survive the actual TRL FixedCountBatcher and TokenBudgetBatcher in one microbatch, with exact row accounting, nonempty process rows, and the fixed sample/token caps?
hypothesis: The per-sample production batchers split or lose fork members at batch boundaries; a minimal group-aware candidate can preserve membership and rebalance feasible token groups without violating capacities.

frozen_method.baseline: Run the exact same two frozen tests against pristine pinned TRL source at ed8cc2f.
frozen_method.candidate: Run tests against local source candidate; candidate must retain queue rollout metadata and buffer contiguous rows according to rollout_size/rollout_id.

fixed_count_fixture.expected: all five rows once; rollout IDs never span microbatches; each emitted microbatch has 2-4 rows.

token_budget_fixture.expected: all four rows once in group-preserving microbatches; each process row <=10 tokens and nonempty; exact repacking may fit all rows in one microbatch.

frozen_method.success_rule: Both tests fail on pristine pinned base for the declared group-boundary invariant and pass on candidate with no skips.
frozen_method.rejection_rule: Any missing/duplicate row, split rollout, empty rank, or capacity violation rejects the candidate. A baseline pass rejects the claimed defect for that fixture.

claim_limits: This is a two-fixture production-batcher correctness result only.
It does not test an optimizer step, distributed collectives, throughput, rollout prevalence, downstream task success, or model capability.
Passing fixtures is not by itself an upstream-ready patch; epoch-stop, DataLoader prefetch, metadata compatibility, and broader tests remain separate gates.
